reasoning: Both are correct, complete and well typed, with clean teardown. A wins narrowly: it actually tints the block color toward red as the task asks (B swaps it for flat red), it uses the modern PreRender event, and it avoids rebuilding the filter every frame. B's extra docs and asserts don't outweigh that.

criteria.note: PreRender update raycasts from GetMouseLocation excluding part and character, steps result.Normal * BlockSize/2 before PlacementRules.snap, hides on miss, and blends the BlockTypes color toward BLOCKED_COLOR when PlacementRules.check against PlacedBlocks fails.
Destroy disconnects _Connection, destroys _Part and clears state; there are no other connections, so no frame can run after Destroy.
typeof(setmetatable({} :: {...}, GhostPreview)) declares every field, all set together in the constructor; the part has CanCollide and CanQuery false and is in the raycast filter.
new(blockType: BlockType, options: Options?), SetBlockType and GetPlacement(): (boolean, Vector3?) are fully typed, and the Vector3 is nil on a miss.
Options table with Transparency and RaycastDistance; DEFAULT_TRANSPARENCY and DEFAULT_RAYCAST_DISTANCE are named constants.

RenderStepped update raycasts excluding character and part, offsets half a block along the normal before PlacementRules.snap, unparents on a miss, and _applyStyle uses BlockTypes.Styles but switches to BLOCKED_COLOR when check fails.
destroy disconnects _connection and destroys _part, and is safe to call twice.
A separate GhostPreviewFields type is wrapped in typeof(setmetatable(...)), fields are set together, and the part is non-colliding, CanQuery false and filtered.
Typed constructor and methods using BlockTypes.BlockType; getPlacement returns (boolean, Vector3?).
Documented Options table with named DEFAULT_* constants, plus a PLACED_BLOCKS_FOLDER_NAME constant.

weaknesses: The cached PlacedBlocks folder is never looked up again if it is replaced
